paper.central_claim: ArtiCAD is the first training-free multi-agent system that generates editable articulated CAD assemblies from text/images; predicting assembly relationships (connectors) at design time rather than assembly time, plus cross-stage rollback and a self-evolving experience store, improves quality over a single-VLM loop and prior methods.
paper.title: ArtiCAD: Articulated CAD Assembly Design via Multi-Agent Code Generation

evidence.quote: evaluated independently by three frontier VLMs: GPT-5.2

evidence.quote: Success (Succ.) is binary (0/1), marking valid compilation with all parts.

gap.author_gap: No method generates editable articulated multi-part CAD assemblies from high-level descriptions; single-part CAD generators lack joints and articulated reconstruction outputs non-editable meshes.
gap.checked_gap: Domain gap is real and neighbors are enumerated (CADCodeVerify, Seek-CAD, EvoCAD, CADEvolve for single parts; SINGAPO, Articulate-Anything, PAct for articulated objects). For the RSI-relevant store there is no named memory/skill nearest neighbor and no argument why a Good/Issue case store beats existing reflection/RAG memories.
gap.lineage: single-part generate-execute-repair CAD loops -> multi-agent CAD with connector contract; generic RAG/Reflexion memory -> Good/Issue partitioned experience store
gap.closest_adjacent: Single-VLM Loop (same backbone) as controlled neighbor; Articulate-Anything (VLM coding articulation over retrieved meshes) as functional neighbor.
gap.residue: Joint/assembly relationship prediction under weak LLM 3D reasoning.
gap.stakes: Late-prediction variant loses 10.8 points of success rate and 0.66 Motion.
gap.method_response: Move relationship prediction to design stage via connector frames; deterministic solver handles alignment.
gap.remaining_gap: Closed chains; store contribution unproven; no human validation; backbone-bounded.
unresolved: Whether the experience store gain would persist on a held-out task stream

G.reason: Opus sides with son55. The articulated-CAD capability gap is concrete and its neighbours are named (single-part CAD code loops, non-editable articulated reconstruction, assembly datasets for given parts); on its own it would merit 3. But the object that brings the paper into this domain, the retained experience store, gets no gap analysis: no case-reuse or experience-memory neighbour (ExpeL/Reflexion-style stores are cited only generically) and no residual bottleneck that the store addresses. 'First'/'unexplored' framing locates a capability, not a non-weight object that was previously fixed.

M.reason: Opus sides with sol. The connector contract is a concrete operation with a separating prediction against the naive alternative (late prediction degrades Motion 3.82 → 3.16 and Succ 100 → 89.2%), and the DESIGN/CODE routing with keep/regenerate partitions is reasoned. Not 4: the conditional-independence/O(1) argument is asserted (independent part generation does not guarantee geometric compatibility), and the store is generic case retrieval whose Good/Issue split is judged by the same VLM pipeline. It makes no prediction that separates it from plain trace RAG.

X.reason: Opus sides with son55. Plan validation, the generate–execute–repair loop, routing, deterministic assembly and FAISS partitions are described. But the store's admission threshold, retrieval k, summary format, dedup/forgetting/versioning, ArtiCAD's own repair and rollback limits, and the validation/judge prompts are not given. The paper has no appendix, so the retention path cannot be reconstructed.

E.measurement.reason: Opus sides with son55. CADPrompt and ACD use standard geometric/joint metrics with worst-case scoring of failures (credible). But every ArtiCAD-Bench number, including all ablations and the store claim, comes from VLM judges only (opus:O03), with no human or ground-truth check. α is 0.58–0.64, below the usual 0.667 floor, yet described as 'robust' (opus:O01). Gemini-3-Pro both judges and powers the Pro row (opus:O02). Succ checks compilation only (opus:O05). Store-ablation deltas (≤0.05 on 1–5) are within plausible judge noise.

E.causality.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. A same-backbone Single-VLM Loop and three single-component ablations exist. The late-prediction ablation is informative. Rollback removal also removes visual validation, the store ablation moves quality negligibly (Detail reversed), runs are single, and budgets are unmatched.

E.holdout.reason: Both seats 1; re-checked. The pipeline is tested on two external benchmarks (CADPrompt, ACD), but the store's construction stream, order and reset are unstated (opus:O04). The only retained-effect test (ablation c) runs on the same self-authored benchmark.

E.statistics.reason: Both seats 1 (A2 ladder): sample sizes and failure rates are given, but there are no seeds, intervals or tests for main or ablation differences. Judge agreement is not run variance.

E.cost.reason: Both seats 1; re-checked. Only Avg. Iter. for ArtiCAD vs no-store. There are no token/API/latency figures, no iteration count for the Single-VLM Loop (capped at 5 retries) and no budget-matched comparison.
